summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and chronic obstructive lung disease, was admitted with worsening shortness of breath, hypoxia, and chills following a suspected aspiration event. She had recently completed treatment for pneumonia and a UTI. Initial management in the MICU included broad-spectrum antibiotics due to concern for hospital-acquired pneumonia. Her condition improved with treatment, oxygen requirements returned to baseline, and she remained afebrile. Sputum culture identified MRSA, leading to de-escalation of antibiotics to vancomycin monotherapy. She was discharged home with a plan for six additional days of IV vancomycin via home health, stable respiratory status, and follow-up arranged with her primary care and pulmonary providers.
